primitives.name: Collective Engagement
primitives.verbatim_quote: Remember that the first thing to be done is not to know that you have some one single star, but to induce as large a number of men as possible to come out and try for the team.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'N': 'dimensionless count of participants', 'S': 'dimensionless measure of individual star quality'}
primitives.assumptions: A larger pool increases likelihood of selecting high-performing individuals; S is not deterministic.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When N approaches zero, selection becomes deterministic but lacks diversity.

layer2.mapping: Models the probabilistic distribution of team talent as a function of recruitment volume and selection criteria.
layer2.telemetry: Number of applicants versus final roster size and performance metrics.

primitives.name: Pre-Season Training
primitives.verbatim_quote: If a start can be made before the spring and a number of men persuaded to put themselves into reasonably good condition by gymnasium and general winter work, so much the better.
primitives.assumptions: Training duration and workload directly correlate with conditioning improvement.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When T < 0, no training occurs; when W → ∞, overtraining risk increases.

layer2.mapping: Maps training input to performance output through a conditioning kernel.
layer2.telemetry: Weekly training hours vs. post-training fitness scores.

primitives.name: Selection Testing
primitives.verbatim_quote: Then the man who is chosen captain should, as soon as the weather and men are in condition for a few trials, make a thorough test of his candidates.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'performance score', 'T_{trial}': 'duration of trial in minutes', 'C_{candidate}': 'candidate index'}
primitives.assumptions: Performance is measurable and comparable across candidates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When T_{trial} → 0, insufficient data for reliable P estimation.

layer2.mapping: Evaluates candidate performance using controlled testing environments.
layer2.telemetry: Trial performance scores and ranking consistency.

reasoning_traces.think:
The primitives form a hierarchical system where collective engagement sets the foundation for talent identification. Pre-season training enhances baseline capabilities, while selection testing evaluates actual performance. These components interact dynamically: increased engagement leads to broader talent pools, which, when properly conditioned, yield higher-quality candidates for testing. The interplay between these primitives creates a feedback loop that optimizes team formation. Failure modes include overreliance on star players (contradicting collective engagement), inadequate training leading to poor performance, and flawed testing protocols causing misidentification of talent. Each primitive's breakdown regime reveals critical thresholds—such as minimal recruitment numbers or insufficient training time—that invalidate the model's predictive power.
